security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by sales-process prose, Markdown examples, or inline filename formatting. remediation.suggestion: Copy the required Introw guidance into a local references file and link to it with a path under this skill directory.

content.value_statement: Sales teams need deal-ready collateral that matches buyer roles and sales stages. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code draft decks, one-pagers, scripts, playbooks, and objection responses.
actual_capabilities: Drafts slide-by-slide sales deck outlines with headlines, body copy, and speaker notes.
Creates one-pagers and leave-behinds for meetings, champions, and events.
Builds objection handling tables with responses, proof points, and follow-up questions.
Structures demo scripts with timing, talk tracks, and interaction points.
Outlines ROI calculators, proposal templates, sales playbooks, and buyer persona cards.
Adapts messaging for technical buyers, economic buyers, champions, and end users.
limitations: It does not verify product claims, metrics, pricing, or customer quotes.
It needs accurate product, buyer, and sales process context from the user.
It does not design finished slide visuals or export presentation files.
It is not a CRM, analytics, or sales engagement automation tool.

use_cases.title: Prepare an AE deal deck
use_cases.description: Create a buyer-specific deck that maps pain, proof, value, implementation, pricing, and next steps to a live opportunity.

use_cases.title: Equip a product marketer
use_cases.description: Turn positioning, proof points, personas, and objections into collateral that sales teams can reuse across funnel stages.

use_cases.title: Ramp a sales enablement lead
use_cases.description: Build playbooks, objection guides, demo flows, and persona cards for onboarding and ongoing rep coaching.

prompt_templates.title: Create a one-pager
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple leave-behind.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a one-page sales leave-behind for [product]. Target [buyer persona] at [sales stage]. Use these differentiators: [list]. Include one proof point and one clear next step.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a pitch deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a structured sales deck.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a 10-slide sales deck outline for [product] selling to [persona]. Include problem, cost of inaction, market shift, approach, product walkthrough, proof, implementation, ROI, pricing, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build an objection guide
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for rep-ready objection handling.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an objection handling guide for [product]. Cover price, timing, competition, authority, status quo, and technical concerns. For each objection, include the real concern, response approach, proof point, and follow-up question.

prompt_templates.title: Assemble a launch playbook
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a complete sales enablement package.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a sales playbook for launching [product] into [market segment]. Include buyer profiles, qualification criteria, discovery questions, demo flow, objection handling, competitive positioning, case study needs, and follow-up templates.

output_examples.input: Request a demo script for a first sales demo to a VP Sales buyer.
output: A timed scene-by-scene agenda for a 30 to 45 minute demo.
Talk tracks that connect each workflow to pipeline, quota, and rep productivity.
Interaction questions that confirm priorities before moving to the next scene.
A closing section with value recap, decision process, and next step options.

output_examples.input: Request an objection handling document for price and competition concerns.
output: A table of common objection statements in buyer language.
Plain responses that acknowledge the concern and redirect to value.
Proof points that support each response without overstating claims.
Follow-up questions that keep the sales conversation moving.

output_examples.input: Request a champion enablement one-pager after a discovery call.
output: A concise recap of the prospect problem, proposed solution, and business value.
Three differentiators written for internal forwarding.
A proof point section and a concrete next step with timing.
Layout guidance for scannable sections and visual hierarchy.

best_practices: Provide real product context, buyer role, sales stage, proof points, and known objections before asking for collateral.
Review generated claims with product, legal, and sales leadership before sharing assets with prospects.
Ask for separate versions by persona or funnel stage instead of forcing one asset to serve every buyer.
anti_patterns: Do not use generic collateral without buyer-specific pain, proof, and next steps.
Do not invent customer metrics, quotes, logos, security claims, or ROI numbers.
Do not bury pricing, implementation effort, or decision steps when the buyer expects clarity.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create sales decks, one-pagers, demo scripts, objection guides, ROI tools, proposals, playbooks, and persona cards.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Sales enablement teams, product marketers, account executives, founders, and revenue leaders can use it to prepare sales collateral.

faq.question: Does it replace sales strategy work?
faq.answer: No. It structures and drafts assets from the strategy, positioning, proof, and sales process that the user provides.

faq.question: Can it create deal-specific materials?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the target account, buyer role, sales stage, known pain, current objections, proof points, and desired next step.

faq.question: Can it generate final slide designs?
faq.answer: No. It creates slide outlines, copy, speaker notes, and layout guidance, but it does not export presentation files.

faq.question: How should teams validate outputs?
faq.answer: Teams should verify product claims, pricing, metrics, customer quotes, legal language, and competitive statements before external use.
